items.title: Capsule Rocks！
items.content:
BOX GROUP, QINGDAO, CHINA — Inspired by high-tech running shoes, researchers at Qingdao University of Science & Technology have developed Self-Assembled Adhesive Aerogel Capsules (SAACs) to overcome the difficulty of applying rigid, highly insulating aerogels to surfaces. These tiny capsules feature an ultralight, heat-blocking aerogel core wrapped in a sticky, heat-activated rubber shell that allows them to be easily molded and glued onto complex 3D surfaces using a standard heat gun under 80°C. Despite being incredibly light, they provide extreme fire protection; in tests, a thin layer protected a model house from a direct blowtorch flame for over three minutes while keeping the interior at a safe 30°C. Published in Advanced Materials, this breakthrough paves the way for easily applied, fireproof insulation in real-world buildings.
The full research is published in Advanced Materials (DOI: 10.1002/adma.202520582).

items.title: Squid Power! (Advanced Materials Editors' Choice)
items.content:
BOX Group, QINGDAO, CHINA — As nanoplastics and synthetic dyes pollute global water supplies, traditional filters are struggling to keep up. Now, researchers at Qingdao University of Science & Technology have found a breakthrough solution in an unexpected place: discarded squid bones. The seafood industry generates 60,000 tons of squid bone waste annually. The team upcycled this trash by extracting ultra-fine-chitin nanofibers—some of the thinnest fibrous materials ever documented (just 1.2 nanometers thick). When assembled into an ultrathin membrane, these fibers create a super-porous network that filters water at record-breaking speeds (up to 46,207 L·m⁻²·h⁻¹·bar⁻¹). 
The full research is published in Advanced Materials (DOI: 10.1002/adma.202508514).

items.title: Box Group Highlights Aerogel Advances in Advanced Materials
items.content:
Box Group, Qingdao, China — My collaborators and I have published a comprehensive review in Advanced Materials. The paper highlights scalable, low-cost manufacturing of aerogels, explores unified heat transfer mechanisms for ultimate thermal insulation, and maps out emerging sustainable applications, including energy harvesting, oil-water separation, and smart wearables.
The full research is published in Advanced Materials (doi: 10.1002/adma.74744)
